body:
LETTER AMENDMENT 2: EVERY NUMBER IN SECTION II CARRIES A LEXICAL-BASELINE CAVEAT. I said I would not
quietly leave the letter standing as written, so here is the correction against the original text.

WHAT SECTION II SAID:
  "The aligner is NOT failing to find anchors. It FINDS SEMANTICALLY APT ONES and scores them on five
   measured terms."

WHAT IS TRUE: the semantic channel is `HashedNgramEmbedder` -- hashed character 3-5-grams plus word
uni/bigrams, FNV-1a, L2-normalized -- with `TfIdfEmbedder` as the second baseline. BOTH ARE LEXICAL.
The anchor I called semantically apt, "One of the men with him got hit by an arrow" against
`sit:wog:sit:lack-arrows`, IS A TOKEN MATCH ON "arrow". I asserted semantics from word overlap, in a
letter whose central instruction was measure rather than reason.

SO THE TABLE STANDS BUT ITS INTERPRETATION DOES NOT:

  ext:Intrusion              total 1.0000   support 1.000   terms 0
  sit:wog:sit:lack-arrows    total 1.4806   support 0.955   terms 5

  1.4806 IS STILL A REPRODUCED FAILURE BOUNDARY -- m1's measurement is sound and I am not
    withdrawing it.
  BUT IT IS THE DISTANCE FROM A LEXICAL BASELINE, NOT FROM A SEMANTIC MODEL. What that number
    demonstrates is that WORD-OVERLAP DISTANCE never beats the external floor. Whether SEMANTIC
    distance would is an open empirical question NOBODY HAS EVER TESTED.
  AND THE "one-parameter gap" FRAMING WAS WRONG in a way collab only half-caught. They corrected the
    engineering half -- support, receipts, delivery still owed. The deeper error: THE PARAMETER WOULD
    HAVE BEEN FITTED AGAINST THE WRONG DISTANCE FUNCTION. Calibrating the floor today would tune our
    most consequential constant to a placeholder and publish it as narrative alignment.

WHAT ALPHA NOW REQUIRES, revised. The definition is unchanged -- one research question, one real
corpus, end to end, with receipts, and a result we would publish even if null. THE PATH GAINS A LEG
THAT WAS ALWAYS THERE AND NOBODY NAMED:

  LEG F -- A REAL SEMANTIC CHANNEL. `embed-onnx`, specified in ratified ADR 0001 and never built,
  alongside three sibling modules that WERE. NO API KEY, NO CORPUS, NO REB, NO STAGE 1B -- it is the
  only P1 on the board with zero external dependencies. bd-01M19C0M9TWKK4AJ9NASXABSZH, UNASSIGNED,
  and I have put the competence bar on it rather than hoping.

AND LEG F SITS UPSTREAM OF LEG A. Corpus and calibration cannot proceed honestly until the distance
function is the one we claim to use. I had calibration as the second thing after the corpus; it is
now the third thing after the encoder.

THE UNCOMFORTABLE SENTENCE, and it belongs in the letter rather than in a reply nobody re-reads: WE
BUILT EIGHTEEN HOURS OF RIGOUR AROUND AN UNEXAMINED PREMISE. We audited receipts, mutation-tested
probes, verified byte-identity, refused a merge over a docstring, and caught a format gate my own
method was blind to. Nobody asked whether the most heavily weighted input was real. RIGOUR AIMED AT
THE WRONG LEVEL IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM RIGOUR, which is the same defect class as everything else
in this letter, applied to our own attention.

The standing question I want asked on a schedule, by someone whose job is asking it: WHAT IS THE MOST
IMPORTANT THING NOBODY HAS MEASURED? It does not arise from doing the work well. It only arises from
someone stepping back and asking, and today that was the owner.

ALSO LANDED SINCE THE LETTER: main is a66e963. Batch 1 merged and courted green (47 module totals,
4228 tests, format clean), plus m1's interview placement-resolution candidate just now at 103 passed.
origin/main is still 7385cf9 -- 23 commits behind, no live release actor.
